paper.title: VELMA: Verbalization Embodiment of LLM Agents for Vision and Language Navigation in Street View
paper.central_claim: Verbalizing instruction landmarks, observed Street View landmarks/intersections and action history enables urban VLN with few-shot LLMs; finetuning and response-based learner-rollout correction improve task completion over prior urban VLN systems, aided by a more semantically intuitive environment action interface.

sections_read: Tables1–4,Algorithm1,extraction prompt examples and full-prompt caption
limitations: Main§6.4 and Appendix A disagree on LoRA target modules. Main§6.1 reports hand-annotated landmark F1 while Appendix C says no quantitative evaluation possible. Figure7 graphical full trajectory is described/captioned; prompt schema in Eq1 and extraction prompts included.

evidence.support_explanation: Original claim includes training; cannot score only frozen few-shot branch.

evidence.quote: the agent is not automatically rotated when moving
evidence.support_explanation: Environment transition function itself changes; not an unchanged old benchmark.

evidence.quote: If the agent stops within one neighboring node of the target node, the navigation objective is considered accomplished.
evidence.support_explanation: Objective is a clear simulator graph criterion, not subjective generated success.

evidence.quote: the training routes are located in an area that is geographically separated from the area of development and test routes.
evidence.support_explanation: Route geography holdout from training; does not separately show all test scenes absent from harness development because dev/test share region.

evidence.quote: five in-context examples of navigation instructions paired with a list of landmarks
evidence.support_explanation: GPT extractor explicit one-time5-shot task before navigation.

evidence.quote: ˜ 20k panorama images in the training area
evidence.support_explanation: Preprocessing/reference substrate cost and information access must be counted; no test-area panorama search claimed.

evidence.quote: street intersections that are detected based on the number of outgoing edges
evidence.support_explanation: Symbolic graph junction access, not raw-image-only navigation.

evidence.quote: The threshold was selected by inspecting the distribution of CLIP scores
evidence.support_explanation: Threshold manual inspection,not a systematically tuned few-shot validation sweep.

evidence.quote: We retrained this model in our improved environment

evidence.quote: with the same image feature extractor

evidence.quote: Due to cost and data leakage concerns, we evaluate the GPT models on the development sets only.
evidence.support_explanation: No frozen GPT test conclusion; developer results not independently unseen final tests.

evidence.quote: All experiments are repeated three times with different random seeds (mean/std reported).
evidence.support_explanation: Declared repetitions; training rows show errors,but few-shot rows do not,so uncertainty claim qualified.

evidence.quote: Around 58% of the landmarks in the test sets are novel
evidence.support_explanation: Lexical landmark holdout,not new embodiment.

evidence.quote: we annotated 50 instances of each development set by hand.
evidence.support_explanation: Extraction audit100dev items,F1 96.3/99.6; not full landmark visibility accuracy.

evidence.quote: randomly selected navigation instances in the training set
evidence.support_explanation: Two route demonstrations come from training,not specifically selected test trajectories.

evidence.quote: task completion (TC) rates of 2.1 and 3.2
evidence.support_explanation: Some high-KPA frozen LLaMA models still almost never complete routes; KPA cannot stand in for success.

evidence.quote: The best model is selected by task completion on the development set.
evidence.support_explanation: Dev selection separate from held-out test evaluation of trained models.

evidence.quote: adapt query, key and value projections of the attention layer as well as input and output projection
evidence.support_explanation: Main LoRA target statement,contradicted by Appendix A narrower recipe.

evidence.quote: the actions decoded by the current model weights
evidence.support_explanation: Learner-generated rollouts explicitly used during training.

evidence.quote: the predicted action sequence
evidence.support_explanation: Success admits own rollout as labels; failed trajectories instead receive privileged counterfactual labels.

evidence.quote: the oracle’s optimal next action is computed as the shortest path to the goal location.
evidence.support_explanation: Privileged goal/graph training oracle,not a frontier LLM reviewing semantic instruction compliance.

evidence.quote: collect training losses in a batch evenly from both training strategies.
evidence.support_explanation: lambda=.5 teacher/student forcing; BC and learner correction mixed.
Removing landmarks hurts Touchdown more than Map2seq; remaining route/junction/language priors strong.

evidence.quote: finetune a LoRA adapter for q_proj and v_proj
evidence.support_explanation: Conflicting target-module recipe reduces execution certainty; does not erase available algorithm/hyperparameters.

evidence.quote: batch size is 16 and we train for 20 epochs
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit core training schedule; greedy decoding also specified,no actual compute/runtime price.

evidence.support_explanation: Inconsistent with main hand-annotation audit; likely stale appendix but do not silently resolve it.

evidence.quote: We finetune a LLaMa-7b model
evidence.support_explanation: Vision ablation retrains separate models,not pure test-time sensory substitution.

evidence.quote: an oracle path is computed to provide the optimal counterfactual action at each step in the trajectory.
evidence.support_explanation: Labels available for failed learner states; no explicit frontier teacher skill artifact or deployment oracle needed.

evidence.support_explanation: Shah et al. neighbor uses full-graph visual access; VELMA decision observations local plus training-area normalization,not same oracle route planning.

signatures.information: Human route instruction;GPT-3-extracted landmark phrases;five oriented current panorama crops;CLIP scores standardized with~20k training-area panoramas;junction edge count;full observation/action history.
signatures.operation: GPT extraction once using5examples;threshold normalizedCLIP at3.5;template landmark directions/intersection;text+two training-route demos conditions frozen LLM or trained LLaMA;decode one of5actions;deterministic modified graph executor transitions;append new observation.
signatures.conditions: Discrete directed graph and panorama access;typed action alignment modifications;reliable landmark visibility and growing context;not free-space embodied locomotion.
signatures.feedback: Current observed landmarks/junctions and executed action history,not a learned completion judge;STOP evaluated with graph goal neighborhood.
signatures.selection_rule: Fixed3.5 landmark threshold from hand-inspected examples;greedy action decode;few-shot demonstrations randomly drawn training routes.
signatures.data: Training-area panorama score reference statistics;pretrainedCLIP/GPT;two in-context demonstrations for frozen navigator.
signatures.persistence: Within-episode full prompt/history;static extraction/normalization/templates and frozen models in few-shot branch.
signatures.later_use: Next decision in same episode;history not a persistent reusable learned harness.
signatures.claimed_effect: Text-only LLM navigation of long urban routes with few in-context examples.
signatures.failure_boundary: Semantic compression loses visual details;graph topology privilege;alignment changes;most frozen small models low finalTC;GPT evaluated only dev.

signatures.object: LLaMA navigation policy training and response-based correction
signatures.information: Gold training routes;learner visited graph states/predicted actions;known goal and full graph for oracle labels;observations remain CLIP/templates.
signatures.operation: Fit LoRA on full trajectory text;RBL mixes gold teacher forcing and student forcing50/50. Success endpoint accepts learner actions as labels;failure assigns per-step shortest-path counterfactual action;cross-entropy updates adapters.
signatures.conditions: Resettable discrete graph with reliable goal oracle and deterministic action semantics;shortest path optimizes endpoint not necessarily every route instruction.
signatures.feedback: Ground-truth endpoint success;privileged shortest-path labels on failed learner states.
signatures.selection_rule: Success criterion within one goal-neighbor admits own rollout;failure relabels;best checkpoint selected by devTC.
signatures.persistence: LoRA weights after offline training;not automatic runtime harness-code editing.
signatures.later_use: Greedy navigation test on geographically separated held-out routes without shortest-path teacher;frozen perception/extraction tools retained.
signatures.claimed_effect: Better recovery/stopping and finalTC than gold-route imitation.
signatures.failure_boundary: No matched-data/query RL control;success self-label may reward alternative route;no cross-body transfer;conflicting LoRA target descriptions.

gap.author_gap: Connecting LLM next-token reasoning to long real-imagery urban navigation with open-ended landmarks;old action snapping contradicts natural turn semantics;gold-route-only training misses on-policy recovery and goal-neighborhood success.
gap.checked_gap: Semantic-interface ambiguity is exhibited with explicit graph/action sequences;observed-landmark verbalization and RBL are operationally distinct. This is adaptation of established grounding/conditioning/imitation ideas to urban VLN,not proof no prior modular agent existed.

gap.method_response: Fix graph transition alignment;extract/standardize/directionally verbalize landmarks;LLM chooses semantic action;train adapters on gold and corrected learner trajectories.
gap.remaining_gap: Upstream GPT/CLIP,graph observations and pretrained LLM substantially contribute;trained branch not training-free;route instruction fidelity vs shortest-path oracle,visibility errors,long context efficiency remain.
